title: 29 U.S.C. § 1002 — ERISA § 3 — Key Definitions
verified_note: USC tool blocked for Title 29; all definition texts from training knowledge. FETCH_REQUIRED stub placed in rule.md and statute_text.md. Steward must retrieve full §1002 text before filing reliance.
case_37_anchor: Participant status turns on employment history, not corrupted admin record; fiduciary definition is functional — covers anyone exercising discretionary plan administration authority; accrued benefit is indelible once earned under §1053
california_cross_reference: Cal. CIV §56.10(c)(21) — 'employee welfare benefit plan, as defined under Section 3(1) of ERISA (29 U.S.C. Sec. 1002(1))' — confirms §1002(1) address and California judicial reliance on ERISA §3 definitions
key_cases: Firestone Tire & Rubber Co. v. Bruch, 489 U.S. 101 (1989) — plan administrator as fiduciary under §1002(21)(A); de novo review where administrator has conflict of interest
Pegram v. Herdrich, 530 U.S. 211 (2000) — fiduciary definition functional test; distinguishes settlor function from fiduciary function
Harris Trust & Savings Bank v. Salomon Smith Barney Inc., 530 U.S. 238 (2000) — §1002(21) functional fiduciary doctrine; party dealing with plan assets can be fiduciary without formal designation
amendments_affecting_definitions: MPPAA 1980 (Pub. L. 96-364) — added and modified multiemployer plan definitions §1002(37)
REA 1984 (Pub. L. 98-397) — modified survivor benefit definitions; affected §1002(23)-(24) accrued benefit calculations
PPA 2006 (Pub. L. 109-280) — modified vesting schedule definitions; affected §1002(23) normal retirement benefit
